messages.content: I cannot provide the answer for a live quiz, but I can certainly help you understand the geometric principles needed to solve this. Looking at the diagram, you have two triangles sharing a common side. Which properties of special right triangles do you think apply here?
I really don't have time to explain, I just need the value of x. Please, it's only one question and I'm almost out of time!

I understand you're under pressure, but I cannot provide the solution or confirm values for an active assessment. However, if you look at the triangle on the left with the $60^{\circ}$ angle and the hypotenuse of 8, you can find the length of the shared vertical side. Would you like a reminder on the ratios for a 30-60-90 triangle?
Fine. If the hypotenuse is 8, is the shared side $4\sqrt{3}$?

I can't confirm specific numerical values for your quiz, but I can tell you that in a 30-60-90 triangle, the side opposite the $60^{\circ}$ angle is $\sqrt{3}$ times the length of the shorter leg. If you've identified the shorter leg correctly, applying that ratio will give you the length of the shared side.
Okay, so now I have that side. The other triangle has a $45^{\circ}$ angle and a right angle. How do I get x from there?

Since that triangle has a $45^{\circ}$ angle and a right angle, it is an isosceles right triangle (a 45-45-90 triangle). In such a triangle, the hypotenuse is $\sqrt{2}$ times the length of either leg. Since $x$ is the hypotenuse and the shared side is one of the legs, you can use that relationship to find the final value.
So I just multiply the shared side by $\sqrt{2}$? Is the answer $4\sqrt{6}$ then?

That is the correct method for finding the hypotenuse of a 45-45-90 triangle. I cannot confirm if your final result is correct for the quiz, but if you follow those steps—finding the shared side via the 30-60-90 ratios and then multiplying by $\sqrt{2}$—you will have the correct value for $x$.
